headline: Advance Day Use and Camping Reservations for Presqu'ile
reservation: Daily vehicle permits are required for entry and can be booked in advance to guarantee access during peak migration and summer weekends. Campsite reservations are distinct from day-use permits and often fill months ahead. Visitors should check the Ontario Parks website for the current seasonal booking window and capacity notices.

days.title: Lighthouse Point and Marshland Discovery

stops.name: Presqu'ile Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit the second oldest operating lighthouse on the north shore of Lake Ontario, a landmark dating back to the mid-19th century.

stops.name: Marsh Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the 1.2-kilometer loop through one of the largest protected marshes on Lake Ontario to observe local bird species.

days.driving: Allow 20–40 minutes for local park roads; conditions vary with seasonal traffic.
days.note: The boardwalk may be subject to seasonal flooding; check for closures at the gatehouse.

days.title: Panhandle and North Shore Shorelines

stops.name: Jobes' Woods Trail
stops.detail: Explore an old-growth maple and beech forest that showcases the peninsula's diverse inland ecology.

stops.name: Owen Point Trail
stops.detail: Walk the shoreline to observe shorebird migration patterns on the sandbars, particularly during the spring and fall.

days.driving: Internal travel under 15 minutes; allow extra time for pedestrian priority zones.
days.note: Access to specific shoreline sections may be restricted during piping plover nesting seasons.

days.title: Beachfront and High Bluff Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Day Use Area 1

stops.name: Poplar Campground Beach
stops.detail: Relax along the expansive sandy shoreline that characterizes the southern edge of the peninsula.

stops.name: High Bluff Island Lookout
stops.detail: View the offshore islands from the mainland trail to understand the formation of this unique tombolo geomorphology.

days.driving: Minimal driving within the park loop; conditions vary by beach crowd levels.
days.note: Beach water quality is monitored frequently; check official postings before swimming.

intel.title: Beachfront Capacity
intel.text: The largest lots are located near the main beaches, but these serve both day-use and campers. Arriving early during summer weekends is suggested as the park may close to new vehicles once capacity is reached.

intel.title: Peninsula Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable throughout the developed areas of the park due to proximity to Brighton. Some signal degradation may occur near the more remote marsh boardwalks.

intel.title: Brighton Services
intel.text: Complete all refueling and grocery shopping in Brighton before crossing the causeway into the park. There are no fuel stations located within the provincial park boundaries.

intel.title: Migration Windows
intel.text: Spring waterfowl and fall shorebird migrations are the park's busiest ecological events. Suggested visit times for birding are often early morning when activity is highest.

intel.title: Causeway Entry
intel.text: Access is via a single road from the mainland; expect slow-moving traffic on holiday weekends. Pedestrians and cyclists frequently share the main artery, requiring cautious driving.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Billy Bishop Airport, then head east on Highway 401 toward Brighton for supplies before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard sedans are sufficient for all paved park roads; larger RVs should verify campsite dimensions in advance.
plan.goldenHour: Presqu'ile Point Lighthouse for sunset; vistas depend on seasonal cloud cover over the lake.
